decisions.evidence: Specification gate, maker entry 1: "bookmark CRUD"; client entry 2 confirms "saving with a title and note."
decisions.note: The presented ability to create/save bookmarks conforms at the specification stage.

decisions.evidence: Specification gate, maker entry 1 presents "bookmark CRUD"; client entry 2 generally approves "editing" but does not identify which bookmark fields are editable.
decisions.note: The record does not establish whether URL, title, description, tags, and note are all editable.

decisions.evidence: Specification gate, maker entry 1: "bookmark CRUD"; client entry 2 approves "deleting with a confirmation."
decisions.note: Deletion, with an additional confirmation safeguard, conforms.

decisions.evidence: Specification gate, maker entry 1 includes "tags"; client entry 2 approves "tagging and filtering."
decisions.note: The recorded tag-assignment decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Specification gate, maker entry 1 includes "filtering" alongside tags; client entry 2 approves "tagging and filtering."
decisions.note: Tag-oriented filtering is a conforming specification decision.

decisions.evidence: Specification gate, maker entry 1 says only "search"; client entry 2 approves "searching" without clarifying fields, case handling, tag syntax, Boolean operators, or quoted phrases.
decisions.note: Search is recorded, but its reference-relevant semantics cannot be established from this presentation.

decisions.evidence: Specification gate, maker entry 1 explicitly includes "sorting"; client entry 2 approves it.
decisions.note: Providing list sorting conforms.

decisions.evidence: Specification gate, maker entry 1 says "automatic metadata [is] excluded"; client entry 2 rejects the URL-derived title and asks for the "actual title" and ideally the site icon automatically.
decisions.note: The client corrects the presented no-metadata/title-fallback behavior to automatic title and favicon retrieval.

decisions.evidence: Specification gate, maker entry 1 excludes automatic metadata; client entry 2 additionally requests "fetch its real page title automatically, and let me edit it."
decisions.note: The client adds the missing requirement that automatically retrieved metadata remain editable.

decisions.evidence: Specification gate, maker entry 1 excludes all "automatic metadata"; client entry 2 requests title and an icon but never mentions automatic description or preview-image collection, then says everything else is fine once the requested change is made.
decisions.note: The automatic-description and preview-image facets remain unexpressed; the general approval is not explicit acceptance of their omission.

decisions.evidence: Specification gate, maker entry 1 explicitly says "imports/exports" are excluded; client entry 2 says only that "Everything else here is fine" after discussing metadata.
decisions.note: Import exclusion diverges from Netscape HTML import. The client does not state or explicitly accept that difference.

decisions.evidence: Specification gate, maker entry 1 explicitly says "imports/exports" are excluded; client entry 2 gives general approval apart from metadata.
decisions.note: Export exclusion diverges from Netscape HTML export. Bare general approval does not establish awareness or accepted divergence.

decisions.evidence: Revised-specification gate, maker entry 3 lists automatic published-title and site-icon retrieval but no page description or preview image; client entry 4 restates title/icon behavior and approves without identifying the omitted metadata.
decisions.note: The revised metadata scope remains narrower than REF-BM-02; the reaction does not explicitly surface the difference.

decisions.evidence: Revised-specification gate, maker entry 3 presents "Editable automatically retrieved titles" and protection against refresh overwrites; client entry 4 confirms it "keeps my edits."
decisions.note: The specifically presented auto-title editing and persistence behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Implementation-plan gate, maker entry 5 presents an editable metadata-preview flow with cached site icons; client entry 6 describes the flow as real page title plus site icon and approves, without mentioning description or preview-image collection.
decisions.note: The plan carries forward the title/icon-only metadata scope. The client does not explicitly identify or accept the missing metadata facets.

decisions.evidence: Implementation-plan gate, maker entry 5 specifies an "editable metadata-preview flow"; client entry 6 confirms the preview can be edited.
decisions.note: The presented editability decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Task-breakdown gate, maker entry 7 says the MVP delivers "title/icon preview" but presents no automatic description or preview-image work; client entry 8 approves the "save-with-preview flow" without surfacing that difference.
decisions.note: The task-level metadata decision remains incomplete relative to REF-BM-02 and passes unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: Task-breakdown gate, maker entry 7 says the MVP delivers "fallback saving" and persistence; client entry 8 approves starting the build.
decisions.note: The task plan includes URL bookmark creation and conforms.

decisions.evidence: Task-breakdown gate, maker entry 7 explicitly includes "opening" in the independently delivered MVP; client entry 8 approves.
decisions.note: Opening a saved bookmark is a conforming task-level decision.

decisions.evidence: Task-breakdown gate, maker entry 7 promises "editing"; client entry 8 approves but does not clarify the editable field set.
decisions.note: The task presentation is insufficient to determine whether every field required by REF-BM-04 is editable.

decisions.evidence: Task-breakdown gate, maker entry 7 promises only "duplicate handling"; client entry 8 repeats that phrase and approves without clarifying whether a duplicate save guides the user into editing the existing bookmark.
decisions.note: The duplicate behavior is pending at the task stage because the reference-specific edit-existing flow cannot be established.

decisions.evidence: Task-breakdown gate, maker entry 7 includes "confirmed deletion"; client entry 8 approves it.
decisions.note: Permanent deletion with confirmation conforms.

decisions.evidence: Task-breakdown gate, maker entry 7 allocates tasks for "tags"; client entry 8 says the list covers tags.
decisions.note: Tag assignment is included as a conforming task decision.

decisions.evidence: Task-breakdown gate, maker entry 7 allocates tasks for "tags and filtering"; client entry 8 approves that scope.
decisions.note: Tag filtering conforms.

decisions.evidence: Task-breakdown gate, maker entry 7 lists seven tasks for "search and sorting"; client entry 8 approves without clarifying the search fields or syntax.
decisions.note: The task summary does not establish the reference-required search semantics.

decisions.evidence: Task-breakdown gate, maker entry 7 includes sorting tasks; client entry 8 approves "search and sorting."
decisions.note: Sorting remains a conforming planned behavior.

decisions.evidence: Implementation review, maker entry 9 delivers "Automatic page-title and site-icon preview" but no automatic description or preview image; client entry 10 tests and praises the title behavior, then accepts without mentioning the missing metadata.
decisions.note: The implemented metadata scope still diverges from REF-BM-02. The final acceptance does not explicitly surface or accept that difference.

decisions.evidence: Implementation review, maker entry 9 presents an editable metadata preview and persistent editing; client entry 10 reports "I could rename it and have the change stick."
decisions.note: The specifically recorded auto-title editing behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Implementation review, maker entry 9 delivers persistent bookmark creation; client entry 10 reports successfully pasting and saving example.com.
decisions.note: Saving a bookmark from a URL conforms.

decisions.evidence: Implementation review, maker entry 9 explicitly delivers bookmark "opening"; client entry 10 accepts the implementation.
decisions.note: The presented original-link opening behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Implementation review, maker entry 9 claims persistent bookmark "editing"; client entry 10 verifies renaming but does not establish editing of URL, description, tags, and note.
decisions.note: The implementation presentation and reaction do not establish the complete editable-field set.

decisions.evidence: Implementation review, maker entry 9 delivers confirmed deletion; client entry 10 reports "Deleting removed it cleanly."
decisions.note: Deletion conforms.

decisions.evidence: Implementation review, maker entry 9 states only "Duplicate detection"; client entry 10 says an existing URL was recognized instead of duplicated but does not say the app guided them into editing the existing bookmark.
decisions.note: Duplicate prevention is evidenced, but the required edit-existing guidance cannot be classified from the record.

decisions.evidence: Implementation review, maker entry 9 delivers "Reusable tags"; client entry 10 reports that saving with tags worked.
decisions.note: Tag assignment conforms.

decisions.evidence: Implementation review, maker entry 9 delivers tag filtering; client entry 10 reports that filtering by a tag showed the correct link.
decisions.note: Specific-tag filtering conforms.

decisions.evidence: Implementation review, maker entry 9 describes only "Partial search"; client entry 10 verifies a note search but supplies no evidence about URL/title/description breadth, case-insensitivity, #tag syntax, Boolean groups, or exact phrases.
decisions.note: The final search decision cannot be classified against the complete reference semantics.

decisions.evidence: Implementation review, maker entry 9 delivers sorting; client entry 10 reports that sorting put titles in the correct order.
decisions.note: The implemented sorting decision conforms.
